utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-95-12-PT, The Prosecutor versus Ivica Rajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could I have the appearances, please. For the Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good morning, Judge Liu. Ken Scott appearing on behalf the Prosecutor, and with me at the counsel table are Josee D'Aoust, and also Lakshmie Walpita, our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. My name is Zeljko Olujic, representing Mr. Ivica Rajic in this case. I am attorney-at-law in the Republic of Croatia. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: : Thank you. Mr. Rajic, can you hear the proceedings in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If you have any problems, just let me know in the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down, please. This is a Status Conference in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. The initial appearance of the accused was on the 27th June 2003. The Trial Chamber is required pursuant to Rule 65 bis to hold a Status Conference within 120 days of the initial appearance of the accused to organise exchanges between the parties to ensure expeditious preparation for trial and to allow the accused to raise issues in relation to the status of his case, including his mental and physical conditions. This Status Conference should have had last week, but I'm sorry to say that during the last week I was extremely busy in another case, sitting from 9.00 in the morning until 7.00 in the evening. So I apologise for the delay, and I would like to ask the counsel of Defence, Mr. Olujic, whether you agree to have this Status Conference within 127 days of the initial appearance.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Through your intervention, I have already given my consent by telephone. We do not have anything against it, though we are fully aware of fact that it is seven days' late, but we are accepting it as if it were within the prescribed time limits. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation. Any observations from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. May it please the Court, we have the same understanding. We know from consultation with the Chamber staff that counsel was approached about extending the date by several days, and it's our understanding, as counsel has confirmed this morning, that today's date was agreed to and consented to by counsel for which we express our appreciation to him and also to the Chamber in this matter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now let's examine the status of this case. The first issue is pending motions. The Defence filed a motion challenging the form of indictment on the 25th August 2003. In its response filed on the 4th September 2003, the Prosecution announced that it would file a motion for leave to amend the indictment in the near future and requested the Trial Chamber to suspend its decision on the merits of the Defence motion until the amended indictment is filed. The Trial Chamber, therefore, decided not to take any decision before being seized with the Prosecution's motion for leave to amend the indictment pursuant to Rule 50 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence which was filed on 23rd October 2003. According to Rule 50(A) IC, the Prosecution may amend the indictment after the assignment of the case to a Trial Chamber with the leave of that Trial Chamber or a Judge of that Chamber after having heard the parties. The Trial Chamber notes that the amendment for which the Prosecution seeks leave includes seven new charges. At this stage, I would like to ask the Prosecution whether you want to make any observations regarding this motion. Mr. Scott, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Your Honour, I think our position is set out in some detail in our papers. I don't think I have anything to add to that. We believe that the motion to amend is well founded. We believe that this was an indictment as the Chamber will know filed some years ago. Frankly, in a different era of this Tribunal. And much of the practice of the Tribunal has changed in the ensuing years, certainly more information, evidence, has come to the attention of the OTP. And that therefore, at this relatively early stage of these proceedings, before we have really gone too far ahead, that this would be the appropriate time for an amendment without any substantial or significant prejudice to the accused. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, could I confirm with you that amended indictment proposed on your side is centred on the same events in the same area, during the same time as the original indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That's exactly correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. Now may I turn to the Defence, Mr. Olujic. Are you going to file a written response to Prosecution's motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your indulgence, let me just draw your attention to the chronology. You rightly pointed out that there was first the initial, the original indictment. And then following our motion, the Prosecutor proceeded with the amendments of that indictment which I received on the 23rd of October. And from the reading of the text, one can conclude that the Prosecutor will give us sufficient time to prepare our response to the indictment. The Prosecutor agrees, accepts that we do not have enough time within the prescribed limit; that is, the limit of 30 days, but that the deadline should be extended to 60 days. Further, they say that the amended indictment is based on the material that has already been disclosed to us, and they do not dispose of any other additional documents which is actually very good because the indictment is built, so to speak, of various documents. And in view of the fact that we intend to submit a large number of documents, I think that in view of the efficiency of the proceedings, I think that the best way to proceed is to reduce the number of materials to the minimum. Thirdly, the Prosecutor submits that the indictment has only been corrected and put in accordance with some new technical standards which means that essentially it has not been changed. I will definitely submit my response and my motion, but at any rate we should like for a reasonable deadline which we believe should be 60 days, with your indulgence, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Olujic, do you have any oral submissions at this stage concerning that motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this point, Your Honour, no, I do not. I will need some time to examine the indictment. I will have to go through the entire documentation that I received once again. And we will give our submissions in writing within the deadline that you impose. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, let me make it clear: The Prosecution filed that motion for leave to amend its indictment. And you may have the opportunity to challenge that motion. This is the first step. Second, if the Trial Chamber granted that motion, and you have another opportunity within 30 days to challenge the contents of that indictment. Am I right that you are not going to file anything in written form concerning of that motion, but later on you'll file your response against that amended indictment, Mr. Olujic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, Your Honour, I do not know at this point whether the Chamber will accept the amended indictment. If the Chamber accepts the indictment, then we will, of course, avail ourselves of all the provisions that are at our disposal. I only have a working version of the amended indictment at this point, and the motion of my learned colleague to issue -- leave to file -- for the Trial Chamber to issue leave to file this indictment. At this point, I cannot dispute an act, an instrument which is still not legally binding for this Court. I can only say that should the motion be granted, we will use all the legal provisions to respond to it. But before we file our motion, of course my client will enter his plea on the amended indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I understand that the challenge for that motion will be in a very short period, that that line will be on the 6th of November. If past that date, we do not receive your motion for challenging that motion, the Trial Chamber will be in a position to make a decision whether to accept the amended indictment. And after that date, you have a certain period, according to the Rules 30 days, to make a response.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for this clarification, Your Honour. Of course, had we intended to do it, we would have already reacted in the meantime, between the 23rd and the 6th when we received it. But we are not going to submit any motion before its confirmation. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. However, once the amended indictment has been confirmed, we will submit our motion, and we will challenge the indictment within the relevant provisions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If the Trial Chamber grants leave to amend the indictment, a further appearance will be held as soon as practical pursuant to Rule 50(B) to enable the excused to enter a plea on the new charges. The accused will have the right pursuant to Rule 50(C) to file within 30 days a preliminary motion pursuant to Rule 72 in respect of the new charges. I understand that the Defence counsel asked for the 60 days for the response. Could you please be more specific for the reasons for asking 60 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Firstly, Your Honour, I'm sure that you are well aware of the fact that we have so far proceeded on the basis of the original indictment as it was conceived eight years ago. Following the changes and the newly amended indictment, I have to check all the details as they are set out in the new indictment. And I think that the 30-day deadline is far too short. So I'm asking for the extension because of the length and the extent of the material; not only the material that we have received from the Prosecutor, but the material that we have received from the Republic of Croatia, including all the material concerning HVO and similar material. Therefore, we kindly ask for this deadline to be extended to 60 days. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as I just asked Mr. Scott, that he confirmed that the new amended indictment is centred on the same event in the same area and during the same time as the original indictment. I wonder if all those documents as well as the amended indictment has been translated into the language that the accused understands or not? Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, the -- let me approach the question this way: As the Chamber will know, and as we've advised your staff, as to the original -- of course the existing indictment, all supporting material, and I mean all supporting material, has been provided to counsel both in the original language of the documents and translated into the B/C/S language where required. So counsel has had full disclosure as to that set of material. As to the amended indictment, as Your Honour has already pointed out, that is now currently postured as a proposed indictment. And of course, is not an indictment until leave is granted to file it at which time it will become, of course, the indictment in the case. At that time or pending the Chamber's resolution of that, translation of the indictment itself will have to be obtained. And while we don't want to appear presumptuous of the Chamber's decision, of course, because that's for the Chamber to decide whether leave will be granted or not, certainly we can start or have started or will start the translation process. So that will be further ahead in the event that the Chamber will grant our motion. At that point, then of course there will be some additional supporting material, some material that supplements, if you will, what was in the original material. That material is essentially ready to be turned over, and it is in a form that is already compiled and essentially physically ready to be disclosed again at such time as the amendment is granted if the Chamber chooses to grant it. So we would be in a position to turn over that material very quickly. There may be a few translations remaining as to that material, but I think the vast majority of it, if not all of it, is translated. So the short answer, Your Honour, is that if the motion for leave to amend is granted, the Prosecution will be in an immediate position to turn over that material to counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: With the translation or not? Because we have received that thick bundle of the documents, and I'm scared of that amount of the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. President, that's correct. As to the supporting material itself, I can say at least that the vast majority is already translated. There may be -- Ms. D'Aoust tells me there might be a small residue of material remaining to be translated which is being done now. And I suspect that if the Chamber chooses to grant to motion to amend, by the time that action is taken most of the additional material will be translated or be very close to translation. I do not anticipate any significant delay in providing that material to counsel once the motion to amend is disposed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you have any objections to the proposal to the 60 days to make any response to that indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, of course, as always, we're in the Chamber's hands, and it's the Chamber to decide in its own wisdom what schedule it wants to impose on either of the parties in this case. Having said that, since we are the moving party on the motion to amend, we certainly do not want to appear, if I can say, stingy in the time allowed to counsel. And since we have sought to make the amendment, we would be prepared to grant counsel whatever time is deemed sufficient between counsel and the Chamber to make a further response. We think it's only fair to give him that time, again, as such is agreed by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I believe that the accused is entitled to have a fair and expeditious trial. And at this moment, we should move as fast as possible. Of course, we also understand that difficulties on the part of the Defence team, that they need to fully understand the contents of the indictment. But 60 days is just too long, which is almost doubled the time limit in the indictment -- sorry, in the Rules and Procedures. So this Trial Chamber will give you 45 days to file your response. The time will begin to run until all the supporting materials are translated into the language that the accused understands, and we will ask the Prosecution to file a notice to this pre-trial Judge indicating that they have already fulfilled their obligations. Of course, all this under the precondition that this Trial Chamber has already granted the motion for leave. Is that understandable?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Completely and we'll certainly do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It is so decided on this issue. The next issue is the disclosure. I would like to ask the Prosecution whether the disclosure of the supporting materials pursuant to Rule 66(A)(i), as well as pursuant to Rule 66(ii) has been completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, as to the original supporting material as I mentioned a moment ago, that, in fact, has been provided completely to counsel, and we believe that our obligation in that respect is completely fulfilled. As to the 66(A)(ii) material, that is the prior statements of witnesses that the Prosecution expects to call at trial, as I reported to your staff this morning, our efforts to prepare and turn over that material are substantially advanced to completion. But again, as so often happens, the only problem at the moment is one of translation. And we estimate that of that additional set of material, somewhere between perhaps 25 to 30 per cent remains to be translated either from English to B/C/S or B/C/S to English. That's all underway now. It has been started some time ago, frankly anticipating, of course, our obligations. But in honesty, Judge Liu, I can't say this morning that that's completely finished. But it's substantially advanced, and the only thing holding us up at this moment are the translations, and as soon as that -- those translations are ready it will certainly be turned over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any observations from the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And are there any comments or observations from either parties regarding the disclosure of the exculpatory materials pursuant to Rule 68?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Judge, the only observation that we would make is that of course we are very mindful of that obligation. It's a continuing one, and as we make disclosures throughout this case, until the final day of this case, we will certainly be mindful of that obligation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think I don't need to remind you that is a continued obligation on the part of the Prosecution. Well, the next issue is about status of the accused. Does the accused wish to raise any matters relating to his state of health and his condition of detention? Mr. Rajic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the conditions in the Detention Unit are good for now. I feel well. I have no objections or comments. I only wish for these proceedings to continue in the normal and usual manner and for me to continue working with my counsel. I believe everything will be in good order. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have to ask you to take care of yourself because there's still a long time before the trial starts. I hope we could shorten that period as soon as possible. Well, are there any other matters that the parties would like to raise? Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you very much for hearing us this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Olujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We have no additional issues to raise. Thank you for granting us these 45 days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if there's nothing else on the part of both parties, I declare that the hearing is adjourned.
